newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Gazprom to be kept as single entity - Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Russia Gazprom to be kept as single entity - Nemtsov.

text.p: Russia's natural gas monopoly Gazprom will remain a single entity, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Monday.
"Gazprom will be kept as a single entity," he told a news conference. Nemtsov was commenting on a decree signed by Prsident Boris Yeltsin earlier on Monday on restructuring monpolies.
Nemtsov said that the basic aim of the government was also to reduce gas prices.
He said the decree on natural monopolies envisaged increasing the government's influence over the giant gas company and strengthening the company's position on international markets.
Gazprom is the world's biggest gas company and a major supplier to Western European markets.
"The richer Gazprom, the richer Russia," Nemtsov said.
Gazprom will have to compete with other companies to exploit new gas reserves in Russia, and conditions will be introduced to help other gas producers in Russia compete with Gazprom.
"We mean equal access to pipelines and equal tariffs for transporting gas," he said.
Nemtsov said it was the government's aim to increase the company's share price, but did not elaborate.
He gave no further details on how these changes, aimed at increasing competition to the Russian gas market, would be achieved.
